# Independent constructor choice

The Java reference and separately authored ASM Core share one API and frozen
callers. The ASM input allocates exactly once before a local null comparison,
then calls either the no-argument or copy constructor and joins. Both original
programs execute and agree before D8 or recovery. The builder uses the JDK's
internal ASM only as a fixture tool and emits Java 8 bytecode; no compiler
original is rewritten. D8 must retain the common new and both initializer PCs.

Both branch polarities and source/SDK Widget declarations are covered. Fresh
JVMs observe class initialization and sticky failures, input/result identity,
partial final stores, mutable constructor reads, exact constructor/observer/
handler failures and Exception versus Error filtering. All generated Java,
original entries, metadata and Exceptions are checked against the ASM input.
